comment: The third-party parts Quillbinder ships, for the daily security watch (tools/security-watch.py, .github/workflows/security-watch.yml). Keep each version in step with the build: a part's 'pin' names the file and the pattern its version comes from, and the suite secwatch (tests/security_watch_tests.py) fails when a version here differs from it. 'tag' is the part's tag in its own repository ({v} = the version; 'sep' when the tag separates the numbers otherwise). 'uses' says what Quillbinder uses the part for (it goes into an issue).

qt.name: Qt
qt.uses: the program on Linux, Windows and Android

components.name: FFmpeg
components.uses: Linux: the media add-ons, which play audio and video documents

components.name: FFmpeg (Windows)
components.uses: Windows: the add-on Extra Video and Audio Formats (since Windows 0.93.0 built by the project, packaging/windows/win-ffmpeg.sh; Qt 6.12.1 for Windows brings 9.0.2, which the add-on no longer uses)

components.name: whisper.cpp
components.uses: the add-on Speech Transcription (Linux, Windows)

components.name: CTranslate2
components.uses: the add-on Translation and Proofreading (Linux, Windows, Android)

components.name: oneDNN
components.uses: the add-on Translation and Proofreading (Linux, Windows)

components.name: sentencepiece
components.uses: the add-on Translation and Proofreading (Linux, Windows, Android)

components.name: OpenSSL
components.uses: Android: the encrypted connections (the check for updates, the add-ons' model downloads)

components.name: Hunspell
components.uses: Windows and Android: the spelling check (Linux uses Ubuntu's package, below)

components.name: zlib
components.uses: packed files, inside Qt's own build (Linux; Windows has its own: the next entry)

components.name: zlib (vcpkg, Windows)
components.uses: Windows: packed files, linked into quillbinder.exe from vcpkg's port (packaging/windows/win-vcpkg.sh pins vcpkg's commit and checks the port's version)

components.name: Monocypher
components.uses: the check of package signatures, inside the program on every system

components.name: libpng (in Qt)
components.uses: PNG pictures, inside Qt's own build

components.name: libjpeg-turbo (in Qt)
components.uses: JPEG pictures, inside Qt's own build

components.name: libwebp (in Qt)
components.uses: WebP pictures, inside Qt's own build

components.name: FreeType (in Qt)
components.uses: fonts, inside Qt's own build

components.name: HarfBuzz (in Qt)
components.uses: the shaping of text, inside Qt's own build

components.name: PCRE2 (in Qt)
components.uses: search with regular expressions, inside Qt's own build

components.name: MD4C (in Qt)
components.uses: reading Markdown, inside Qt's own build

components.name: Qt PDF
components.uses: showing PDF files (the PDF preview and the PDF files of Help) on Linux, Windows and Android
components.note: Since Qt 6.12 Qt PDF is released with Qt WebEngine as a Qt Extensions module with a version of its own (QB_QTPDF_VERSION in CMakeLists.txt); a patch release of it can bring Chromium's and PDFium's security fixes apart from Qt's own releases. Qt's list of known vulnerabilities (module qtpdf) is read through the entry "Qt" as before.

components.name: PDFium (in Qt PDF)
components.uses: showing PDF files, inside Qt PDF (Linux)
components.note: PDFium has no releases of its own and its repository (pdfium.googlesource.com) is not on GitHub. It is the revision 1afaa1a380fcd06cec420f3e5b6ec1d2ccb920dc inside Chromium 140.0.7339.264, which Qt WebEngine 6.140.0 (the source of Qt PDF here) is based on. No database the watch reads names PDFium itself: the entry watches Chromium's tags (newer releases only) and the GitHub advisories of that repository; PDFium flaws reach the watch through Qt's list of known vulnerabilities (module qtpdf) and are not otherwise found. OSV is not asked (it has no entry for a Chromium commit).

components.name: ggml (in whisper.cpp)
components.uses: the add-on Speech Transcription (Linux, Windows): the compute library inside whisper.cpp
components.note: whisper.cpp v1.9.5 carries its own copy of ggml (ggml/CMakeLists.txt: version 0.26.0, synchronized from the ggml commit ffa4e8b80930029a35991f94e7c8a93cd67730ab, which is not a release of ggml). The watch follows ggml's releases from v0.26.0 on. OSV is not asked: a flaw of ggml is mostly filed with llama.cpp or whisper.cpp, which the watch reads for whisper.cpp.

components.name: Botan
components.uses: the encryption built into the program (OpenPGP through RNP), linked statically (0.99.0; the pack crypto)

components.name: RNP
components.uses: the encryption built into the program (OpenPGP), linked statically (0.99.0; the pack crypto)
components.note: RNP 0.18.0 was withdrawn by its makers; 0.18.2 was not tagged when this entry was made.

components.name: sexpp (in RNP)
components.uses: the encryption built into the program: RNP's S-expression library, a submodule of RNP at the commit RNP 0.18.1 names, linked statically (0.99.0)

components.name: json-c
components.uses: the encryption built into the program: RNP reads and writes JSON with it, linked statically (0.99.0; the pack crypto)
components.note: json-c's tags carry the date of the release (json-c-0.19-20260627): a newer release has another date and is not named as a newer release by this watch; its advisories and OSV are read as for the others.

components.name: bzip2
components.uses: the encryption built into the program: RNP reads bzip2-compressed data with it, linked statically (0.99.0; the pack crypto)
components.note: bzip2's own repository is on GitLab, which the watch does not read; this is the libarchive project's GitHub mirror of it (tag bzip2-1.0.8, the same release).

components.name: zlib (in the encryption libraries)
components.uses: the encryption built into the program: RNP packs and unpacks data with it, linked statically (0.99.0; the pack crypto)

components.name: QtKeychain
components.uses: the program: keeps the passwords of the built-in encryption in the system's key store (0.99.0)

components.name: ONNX Runtime
components.uses: the engine packages of the AI add-ons (Linux): Microsoft's prebuilt library, loaded at run time (0.99.0; the pack onnxruntime)

components.name: ggml (AI engine)
components.uses: the engine packages of the AI add-ons (Linux): the compute library under whisper.cpp, llama.cpp and qwentts.cpp (0.99.0; the pack aiengine)
components.note: Another entry ("ggml (in whisper.cpp)") follows the copy inside whisper.cpp 1.9.5 of the add-on Speech Transcription; this one is the ggml of the new AI engine pack, which whisper.cpp 1.9.6 and llama.cpp use as a system library.

components.name: whisper.cpp (AI engine)
components.uses: the engine packages of the AI add-ons (Linux): speech recognition on the pack's ggml (0.99.0; the pack aiengine)

components.name: llama.cpp
components.uses: the engine packages of the AI add-ons (Linux): language models and speech synthesis (libllama and libmtmd), tag b12808 (0.99.0; the pack aiengine)
components.note: llama.cpp has no version numbers: its releases are the build tags b<number>, here the number.

components.name: qwentts.cpp
components.uses: the engine packages of the AI add-ons (Linux): speech synthesis with Qwen3-TTS, pinned by commit (it has no release tags) (0.99.0; the pack aiengine)

components.name: Sonic
components.uses: the engine packages of the AI add-ons (Linux): changing the speed of speech, pinned by commit (its last release tag, release-0.2.0, is older) (0.99.0; the pack aiengine)

components.name: AppImage runtime (type2-runtime)
components.uses: the program's AppImage on Linux: the small program in front of the packed files (it links libraries of its own)
components.note: Its releases are named by their date. Flaws in the libraries it links in (zlib, squashfuse, zstd) are not named by any database the watch reads under the runtime's name.

ubuntu.comment: The Ubuntu 24.04 source packages whose libraries the AppImage carries, at the versions it was built with (resources/licenses/index.json, the entries with a 'package').
